summary: Host only: nothing was built into an image, flashed, run on or read from the phone, and no decision was requested (0018 is not asked). The NAT-030/033 model was found to lack the loader's inputs (zero ADT, no Video/CommandLine, deviceTreeLength 0x4000); loader_inputs.py builds them as loader.c does and the model's checkpoint-11 arrival still equals the run-009 hardware values. A resume of the payload kernel from a C-checkpoint stop was specified (cresume.c_resume) and run in the model: a chain cp5 -> 11, 30-35, 12, 40-44, 13-16 (17 stops) ends in the same kernel state (entry state, registers, RAM) as an uninterrupted run, with no read of a clobbered register; each omitted primitive is detected. The model also showed that the loader as built writes the whole MPIDR_EL1 into the boot CPU's ADT reg, which the kernel's ml_get_cpu_number_local never matches (MPIDR & 0xffff), so a run past checkpoint 15 reaches the kernel's assertion panic in cpu_init; the masked value passes.

established: In the model the kernel reaches C checkpoint 11 with the loader's ADT and boot_args at the values run 009 measured for x0..x3, TTBR0 (private), TTBR1, TCR and VBAR (SCTLR differs in bits 5 and 7 only, as before)
loader_jump changes only TTBR0_EL1, the loader_return_entered flag, x0..x3 and the x29/x30 frame in the model; x18, x19..x28, SP, TCR, SCTLR, TTBR1, VBAR, MAIR and DAIF are unchanged at the stop

The resume (stub-owned save of SP/x18/x19..x28/SCTLR, flag clear and slot[2] by PA, restore, kernel TTBR0 through _set_mmu_ttb, return through the loader_jump early-return epilogue) gives the kernel back in the state of an uninterrupted run over 17 consecutive stops up to checkpoint 16
Each primitive is needed: flag and slot (no further stop), SP (fault), x19..x28 and x18 (state differs; the kernel reads poison), TTBR0 (state differs; not observable otherwise through checkpoint 16)

TTBR0_EL1 is written only by _set_mmu_ttb (callers common_start, arm_vm_init, pmap_switch_internal, pmap_clear_user_ttb, pmap_clear_user_ttb_internal) and _loader_jump; between the start code and arm_vm_init+0xc18 it is constant

loader.c writes the whole 32-bit MPIDR_EL1 into the boot CPU's ADT reg; the kernel's ml_get_cpu_number_local compares phys_id with MPIDR_EL1 & 0xffff; in the model the lookup fails into machine_routines.c:1335 (cpu_id <= ml_get_max_cpu_number()) inside cpu_init after checkpoint 15, and succeeds with the masked value
The NAT-033 README claim that the model builds boot_args and the ADT as loader.c does was overstated; a correction note was added
